label: Bible Study
prompt: How sweet are thy words unto my taste! yea, sweeter than _____ to my mouth!
verse: How sweet are thy words unto my taste! yea, sweeter than honey to my mouth!
note: Scripture as dessert — Ezekiel said the same after eating a scroll that tasted like honey.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: Ye shall not need to fight in this battle: set yourselves, stand ye still, and see the _____ of the LORD with you, O Judah and Jerusalem: fear not, nor be dismayed; to morrow go out against them: for the LORD will be with you.
verse: Ye shall not need to fight in this battle: set yourselves, stand ye still, and see the salvation of the LORD with you, O Judah and Jerusalem: fear not, nor be dismayed; to morrow go out against them: for the LORD will be with you.
note: Judah's orders: don't fight — stand still and watch. The enemy armies ended up turning on each other.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And Jonathan stripped himself of the _____ that was upon him, and gave it to David, and his garments, even to his sword, and to his bow, and to his girdle.
verse: And Jonathan stripped himself of the robe that was upon him, and gave it to David, and his garments, even to his sword, and to his bow, and to his girdle.
note: Jonathan, heir to the throne, gave David his robe, sword, and bow — handing over the prince's things to his friend.

label: Deep Water
prompt: Awake, O sword, against my shepherd, and against the man that is my fellow, saith the LORD of hosts: smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be _____: and I will turn mine hand upon the little ones.
verse: Awake, O sword, against my shepherd, and against the man that is my fellow, saith the LORD of hosts: smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered: and I will turn mine hand upon the little ones.
note: Jesus quotes this on the night before the cross, foretelling the disciples' flight (Matthew 26:31).

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: And without _____ great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifest in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen of angels, preached unto the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up into glory.
verse: And without controversy great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifest in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen of angels, preached unto the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up into glory.
note: 'Without controversy' — no argument here — great is the mystery of godliness, summed up in six crisp lines about Christ.
